statement: If a number be the least that is measured by prime numbers, it will not be measured by any other prime number except those originally measuring it.
heath_proof: For let the number A be the least that is measured by the prime numbers B, C, D; I say that A will not be measured by any other prime number except B, C, D. For, if possible, let it be measured by the prime number E, and let E not be the same with any one of the numbers B, C, D. Now, since E measures A, let it measure it according to F; therefore E by multiplying F has made A. And A is measured by the prime numbers B, C, D. But, if two numbers by multiplying one another make some number, and any prime number measure the product, it will also measure one of the original numbers; [VII. 30] therefore B, C, D will measure one of the numbers E, F. Now they will not measure E; for E is prime and not the same with any one of the numbers B, C, D. Therefore they will measure F, which is less than A: which is impossible, for A is by hypothesis the least number measured by B, C, D. Therefore no prime number will measure A except B, C, D.
ai_proof_text:
9.14
**Statement:** If a number be the least that is measured by prime numbers, it will not be measured by any other prime number except those originally measuring it.

**Step 1.** Let A be the least number that is measured by the prime numbers B, C, D. I say that A is not measured by any other prime number except B, C, D.

**Step 2.** For, if possible, let A be measured by a prime number E which is not the same as any one of B, C, D.

**Step 3.** Since E measures A, let E measure A according to F, so that E multiplied by F makes A (D7.15).

**Step 4.** Now B measures A, and A is the number made by E and F multiplying one another. But if two numbers by multiplying one another make some number, and any prime number measure the product, it also measures one of the original numbers (7.30). Since B is prime and measures A, B measures one of E, F.

**Step 5.** But B does not measure E. For E is prime, and is therefore measured by an unit alone (D7.11); B, being prime, is a number and not an unit, and by hypothesis B is not the same as E; therefore B cannot measure E.

**Step 6.** Therefore B measures F. In the same way, since C and D are prime numbers each measuring A, and neither of them is the same as E, each of C, D measures one of E, F (7.30) but does not measure E (D7.11); therefore each of C, D measures F. Thus F is measured by B, C, D.

**Step 7.** Now, since E multiplied by F makes A, F multiplied by E also makes A (7.16); therefore F measures A according to E, so that F is a part of A (D7.3). And E, being prime, is not an unit, so that A is made up of F taken more than once; therefore F is less than A (CN5).

**Step 8.** Thus F, which is less than A, is measured by the prime numbers B, C, D. But A was by hypothesis the least number measured by B, C, D; which is impossible.

**Step 9.** Therefore no prime number other than B, C, D measures A. Hence, if a number be the least that is measured by prime numbers, it will not be measured by any other prime number except those originally measuring it. Q.E.D.
